title: Why time crawls in class but flies when you're gaming
beats: He was stuck in class staring at the clock, and it said 1:03.
So he stared it down, looked away for ages, even shook his watch, and it was 1:04.
You see, when you're bored, your brain counts every single second, so time drags.
But that night he started gaming, his brain got too busy to count, and when he blinked, it was 3am, with class in five hours.
hook: 0-2s: cold open mid-action, he's already slumped on his chair in class glaring at the wall clock (no spoken question, Xavier 2026-11-14)

staging.attempts: 1 stare-down (lean in, squint at the clock), 2 look away (turn to the window, drum fingers, look back fast), 3 shake the wristwatch next to your ear. Clock: 1:04.
staging.brain_hq: little you at a desk with a big hand counter, clicking every single second ONE... TWO... yawning, a tall stack of ticked-off seconds beside him.
staging.payoff: your bedroom at night, controller in hand, glued to the screen. Cut to HQ: the counter guy has turned round and is watching the game on the HQ screen too, counter forgotten. Back in the room you blink, the bedside clock flips to 3:00 AM, your face drops.
